newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to hold general election on October 20.
newsitem.headline: Japan to hold general election on October 20.

text.p: The cabinet of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday formally set October 20 as the date for Japan's general elections, a government official told reporters.
Hashimoto earlier on Friday dissolved the Lower House of parliament. Elections for the 500-seat Lower House will be the first since July 1993.

The polls will be the first under a system designed to make campaigning less costly and reduce graft. In place of the old multi-seat system, 300 seats will be decided on a first-past-the-post basis, with the other 200 selected by proportional representation.

Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party -- the biggest in the three-party ruling coalition -- favoured going before voters as early as possible before April, when a rise in an unpopular sales tax takes effect. The tax is to be raised to five percent from the current three percent.
Hashimoto is expected to pin his hopes for a second term in office on an improving economy and his handling of a bitter dispute with the southern prefecture of Okinawa over U.S. military bases there.

The opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) plans to attack the government for imposing the sales tax rise and offer its own plan for a drastic overhaul of the tax system and to cut bureaucratic red tape.
